title: LinkedIn Introduces a 'Seems Like AI Slop' Button - Slashdot

content_html:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from 404 Media: LinkedIn, a social network awash with long AI-generated posts from executives and other corporate workers, has introduced a new button that users can click to flag if a post "seems like AI slop," according to 404 Media's own tests. If you have been anywhere near LinkedIn in the past couple of years, you have undoubtedly seen users posting blatantly AI-generated missives. Often these posts take some sort of news event, and opine on how this relates to thought leadership, or some other LinkedIn brainrot term. It's also pretty wild the button specifically uses the term "AI slop" and not, say, "It seems this was generated with AI."

[...] After publication of this piece, Hari Srinivasan, chief product officer at LinkedIn, wrote their own post about the button. "AI slop is a top priority for all of us. We really care about this. People come to LinkedIn to connect with real people and share their real perspectives, ideas and expertise. Here are a few more changes to keep it that way," he wrote.

The button in part will help LinkedIn tune its own models for identifying AI slop. "We are ramping up a series of new and improved classifiers that identify if a post is AI-slop or generally low-quality content. This will reduce the amount of AI slop you might see in suggested content and content from outside your network," the post said. "We are ramping the ability for members to tell us if they believe a post or comment seems like AI slop. Slop is hard to define and the definition changes; this lets us tune our models and make better feeds." Srinivasan also said LinkedIn is removing the AI-powered "enhance your post" feature with another that "proofreads your words, but does not change your voice."

content_html_zh: 一位匿名读者引用了 404 Media 的一份报告：LinkedIn 是一个社交网络，里面充斥着来自高管和其他企业员工的 AI 生成的长帖子，根据 404 Media 自己的测试，LinkedIn 推出了一个新按钮，用户可以点击该按钮来标记帖子是否“看起来像 AI 过时”。 如果你在过去几年里去过 LinkedIn，你无疑会看到用户公然发布人工智能生成的邮件。 这些帖子通常会涉及某种新闻事件，并就其与思想领导力或其他 LinkedIn 脑残术语的关系发表看法。 该按钮专门使用术语“AI slop”，而不是“这似乎是由 AI 生成的”，这也很疯狂。 [...] 这篇文章发表后，LinkedIn 首席产品官 Hari Srinivasan 撰写了自己关于该按钮的文章。 “人工智能问题是我们所有人的首要任务。 我们真的很关心这个。 人们来到 LinkedIn 是为了与真实的人联系并分享他们的真实观点、想法和专业知识。 为了保持这种状态，还有一些改变，”他写道。 该按钮在一定程度上将帮助 LinkedIn 调整自己的模型来识别 AI 溢出。 “我们正在推出一系列新的和改进的分类器，用于识别帖子是否是人工智能垃圾或普遍低质量的内容。 这将减少你在建议内容和来自网络外部的内容中可能看到的人工智能溢出量，”该帖子称。 “我们正在增强会员告诉我们他们是否认为某条帖子或评论看起来像是人工智能废话的能力。 坡度很难定义，而且定义也发生了变化；这让我们能够调整模型并做出更好的反馈。” 斯里尼瓦桑还表示，LinkedIn 正在删除人工智能驱动的“增强你的帖子”功能，并使用另一个“校对你的文字，但不会改变你的声音”的功能。
